title: test_qos_wrr_floor_zero_share passes vacuously — weights command rejected by MAX_WEIGHT and swallowed, single-residential fixture makes all email unroutable, assertion passes on streaming alone
detail: {100,1,1} exceeds MAX_WEIGHT 64 -> Invalid_Weights, swallowed by submit_c, so the pipe keeps default {1,4,1} and Standard gets cap 3, never the claimed zero share. The fixture has one residential, so Residential->Residential email is src==dst unroutable; no email packets exist. total_del>0 comes from streaming via the normally-allocated Standard lane. The E7 floor-quantum branch is never exercised.
recommended_fix: Use weights within the domain (e.g. {64,1,1}, which does zero Standard at cap 5), tfail on submit_c error, and give the fixture two residentials so email actually spawns; assert on email deliveries specifically.

title: test_severance_reroute_with_alternative cannot distinguish reroute-survival from drop-all — the severance-drop counter is captured then explicitly discarded
detail: The comment claims mid-edge packets must survive the reroute, but the only assertion is deliveries-increase over 20 post-demolish ticks at 30 spawns/tick through the alternative path — that passes even if every mid-edge packet dropped. The drop counter that could discriminate is captured and discarded.
recommended_fix: Assert on the severance drop count around the demolish tick (e.g. fewer .Severance drops than the mid-edge occupancy measured by on_pipe_count), so reroute-survival is required, not just continued fresh deliveries.

title: Five tests discard the catalog-load error (cat, _ := must_catalogs()) — a load failure proceeds with a partially-filled catalog and panics in run_init instead of failing with the named error
evidence:
core/determinism_test.odin:84:
	cat, _ := must_catalogs()
core/determinism_test.odin:108:
	cat, _ := must_catalogs()
core/flow_edge_test.odin:141:
	cat, _ := must_catalogs()
core/flow_test.odin:163:
	cat, _ := must_catalogs()
core/flow_test.odin:203:
	cat, _ := must_catalogs()
core/catalog.odin:185 (the error-return shape):
		if e != nil { return cat, {"packet_types.json", "$", "invalid JSON"} }
core/catalogs_testkit.odin:16-19:
must_catalogs :: proc() -> (^Catalogs, Catalog_Error) {
	src: Catalog_Sources
	test_catalog_sources(&src)
	return catalogs_load(&src)
}
detail: catalogs_load returns the partially-filled cat alongside the error; discarding it means a broken data file leads run_init/bootstrap_map to index empty cat.node_types / cat.packet_types (bounds panic) rather than a clean tfail naming file/field/rule. Sibling fixtures (flow_fixture, severance_fixture, health_fixture, test_boot_state) do check err.file.
recommended_fix: Check the error in these five tests the same way (if err.file != "" { tfailf(t, "catalogs: %s %s %s", ...) }) before run_init.
